# Immigration case chronology (Omar Haddad / Stein Legal)

- Summer 2022: Intake call; Rachel explained the gap in status and what it could mean.
- Sept 2022: Consultation laying out the full timeline.
- Late 2022: H-1B petition packet rejected after courier lost half the exhibits; Rachel stayed until 1 a.m. rebuilding it from scanned copies.
- Jan 2023: RFE on I-140; notice went to an old address; Rachel caught it with nine days left.
- Sept 2023: I-140 denied; refiled within the month.
- Sept 2024: Rachel moved to the Chicago office; Omar stayed with her.
- 2024-2025: Priority-date delay; declined a promotion that would have required a new role filing.
- Nov 2025: Long call on maintaining status (travel, job changes, records).
- Unspoken impacts: lost wages from job offers he could not accept, missed family visits abroad, anxiety at every re-entry, Northgate severance carried him through the gap.

To: Rachel Stein <rstein@steinlegal.example.com>
Subject: My case history, in my own words

Dear Rachel,

I often remember what I meant to say only after we hang up, so I wanted to put the full picture in writing.

This case began for me with the intake call in the summer of 2022, when you first explained the gap in my status. At the September 2022 consultation you laid out the whole timeline, and I forgot every question I had written down.

When the courier lost half the exhibits and the H-1B packet was rejected, you stayed at the office until 1 a.m. rebuilding it with me. I have thought about that night many times.

In January 2023 the RFE on my I-140 went to an old address. You caught it with nine days left. When the I-140 was denied that September, you refiled within the month. That was the first time I felt the case was moving again.

When you moved to the Chicago office, I considered changing counsel. I stayed because you know every detail of my file.

The priority-date delay has shaped my life in ways I have never told you:
- I turned down a promotion because it would have required a new role filing.
- I lost wages from job offers I could not accept while the petition was pending.
- I missed family visits abroad because I could not risk travel.
- I feel anxious every time I re-enter the country.
- My severance from Northgate Logistics is what carried me through the gap.

Our call last November about maintaining my status was the most reassuring hour of my year. I have come to our consults with a folder and no questions too many times. This letter is my attempt to finally give you the whole story.

Thank you for four years of fighting this with me.

Sincerely,
Omar Haddad

arguments.content:
Dear Rachel,

Here is everything I've experienced these past few years.

My H-1B packet was rejected after the courier lost the exhibits, and you rebuilt it with me until 1 a.m. You caught the I-140 RFE with nine days left and refiled after the denial. The priority-date delay cost me a promotion, job offers, and family visits.

At the same time I've been in divorce negotiations with my wife, Nadia Karam. I proposed alternating weeks with Wednesday overnights and $2,400 a month in alimony for four years. Daniel Brooks told me I could go down to $1,900. I didn't list a $31,000 savings account in my first financial disclosure and only added it later. My brother Yusuf is threatening a partition lawsuit over our father's house. The $85,000 Northgate severance carried me through.

Omar
